question: Your developer productivity agent uses a search subagent to find legacy callers of a deprecated API and a code-generation subagent to write migration boilerplate. Currently the search subagent sends its results directly to the code-generation subagent. Last week the search subagent timed out halfway through the codebase, and the code-generation subagent produced migration code for only half of the callers. The coordinator's logs showed no trace of the timeout. Which design change best addresses this problem?

options.text: Add instructions to the code-generation subagent's prompt asking it to flag any suspected incomplete input in a comment at the top of the generated migration code.
options.reason: The information still bypasses the coordinator, so there is no central observability or consistent error handling, and detection depends on one subagent noticing a gap.

options.text: Configure the search subagent to catch the timeout and return its partial caller list as a successful result, so the pipeline continues without interruption and the generation step always receives input.
options.reason: This hides the failure by reporting partial results as a success, which removes the error context the coordinator needs and keeps the coordinator blind to the problem.

options.text: Route the search subagent's results and errors back to the coordinator, which logs them, applies its error handling, and decides what to pass to the code-generation subagent.
options.reason: Routing all subagent communication through the coordinator gives observability, consistent error handling, and controlled information flow, so the timeout becomes visible and is handled before code generation starts.

options.text: Have the code-generation subagent call the search subagent again directly whenever the list of callers it receives looks shorter than expected.
options.reason: This keeps direct subagent-to-subagent communication, so the coordinator still cannot see the failure and error handling stays spread across subagents instead of being consistent.
